Supper at the Inn:
Setup
quiet, domestic, faintly foreboding
the first scene of the story, opening Arc I and its Chapter 1
Before 'The Stranger' and later 'The Betrayal', it simply places Norman, Alice and Bob together at the inn and notes the Sword of Ash.
The Betrayal:
Turn
somber, bitter, quietly final
midway through the story, the last scene of Arc I closing its third chapter
After 'The Stranger' leaves Alice and Bob laughing together, this breaks their friendship, reversing their bond before 'Gathering Storm'.
darker than the two scenes before it.
Gathering Storm:
Escalation
quiet, tense, foreboding
early in Arc II, opening Chapter 4
After 'The Betrayal' breaks the friendship, this shows pressure building over Ashford before 'The Fall of Ashford' destroys it.
quieter than 'The Betrayal', trading heartbreak for foreboding.
The Fall of Ashford:
Climax
bleak, violent, final
the last scene of Arc II, closing Chapter 5 and the whole story
After 'Gathering Storm' foreshadows the coming storm and 'The Betrayal' breaks bonds at the inn, 'The Fall of Ashford' enacts the town's destruction that resolves the arc.
darker and more final than 'The Betrayal' and 'Gathering Storm'.
